data.title: Coming next year: Medicare Advantage plans without drug coverage for almost 640,000 people and fewer choices for the rest
data.description:
By Beth Pinsker

Medicare Advantage is starting to lose its all-in-one benefit

Before you buy, make sure your Medicare Advantage plan has Part D coverage.

Prescription drugs have always been a standard offering of Medicare Advantage plans, but not anymore.

During this open enrollment season for 2027, when 70 million Medicare enrollees should be shopping for next year's coverage, many will find out that their plans are dropping Part D drug coverage as part of their bundled services. For 2027, beneficiaries in 193 counties will have no Medicare Advantage plans with Part D coverage available, KFF found. That's about 638,000 people, up from 399,000 uncovered beneficiaries in 2026.

Beneficiaries in most counties still have Part D options, but fewer of them. Most places in the U.S., particularly rural areas, have reduced included Part D options for 2027, with a net drop of over 1,600 plans among the top 10 providers. Only one company, Devoted Health, is adding plans for 2027. (Neither the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services nor Devoted Health responded to requests for comment.)

"It's a mess out there this year," said Marcia Mantell, an independent Medicare consultant and author of the book, "Creating Your Medicare Recipe."

Retirement experts have long quibbled over the name "Medicare Advantage" for the insurance program that about half of all Americans over 65 choose to cover Medicare copays and other uncovered costs. Many critics make a play on words and call it "disadvantaged," mostly because out-of-pocket spending can end up higher than the alternative, which is traditional Medicare with a supplemental health insurance plan, despite having a zero or low monthly premium.

If there has been an "advantage" to Medicare Advantage, it has been that the HMO-like coverage provides bundled services that traditional Medicare doesn't cover: vision, hearing and dental. Plus, plans typically offer perks such as gym memberships, grocery stipends or other cash refunds.

When a Medicare Advantage plan does not offer something as essential and potentially costly as Part D drug coverage, an enrollee in the plan would have to find that coverage elsewhere, putting them in the same position as those who choose the traditional Medicare route and purchase supplemental insurance plans for Part B and Part D. That could average about $51 a month in 2027 for the drug plan, according to a KFF analysis.

"The costs have gone up so much and the nitpicking is in the details," said Katy Votava, a Medicare expert and author of "Making the Most of Medicare: A Guide for baby boomers." "A lot of plans are being canceled and that scares people. Then they have to make a choice of where they're going next."

The help for that process is especially lacking this year, said Votava, whose independent Medicare consulting company is called GoodCare. For one thing, she's hearing about a lack of availability of local counseling services through the free State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP). "A couple called me the other day because they can't get in to see a SHIP counselor," she said.

Another impediment is that professional counselors are not getting the same kind of commissions as in the past for the work they do on Part D drug plans. "It makes it impossible for the broker to help," Votava said. Enrollees with questions who seek hired help then can't afford what they need without that commission structure covering part of the cost. "People talk to me when they're already in a mess. I charge $400 an hour. Not everyone has a lot of money," Votava said.

If clients come to Votava and don't have it in their budget to pay the fee and no commission is available, she does her best to point them in the right direction. One hospital in Minnesota used to list her as a Medicare information resource, she said.

Changes ahead?

With the new Congress coming in 2027, there are possibilities for change, but Votava said that not much can be done for the coming year's plans because those are already set. Open enrollment doesn't close until Dec. 7, allowing time to shop.

But it means really doing the work, not just picking the same plan as last year. Votava said many people throw up their hands in frustration and don't spend much time on the process - 27% don't check it at all, and 33% spend less than an hour, according to a University of Michigan study.

It takes bargain hunting and attention to get the job done, but not necessarily an advanced degree in healthcare policy.

"If you can shop for shoes online, you can shop for Medicare," said Votava. "Medicare.gov has really improved. It auto-populates medications. You just have to double-check it."

Retirees will do best if they know the pitfalls - like noticing a shoe retailer that used to offer free shipping suddenly rescinds that offer without making it apparent.

"If you're going to take a $0 premium Medicare Advantage plan, look carefully," she said. "You need a drug plan. It's dangerous not to have one."

You may have to shop for a Part D plan. You may also need your own gym membership and maybe even your own dental and vision discount plans, depending on the plan you choose. Votava has heard that many more plans are dropping Silver Sneakers, a popular gym plan.

"They might have had it included with their plans for years, but now there are changes and they might not be able to use that benefit. That's another pressure that consumers aren't aware of," Votava said. "It's definitely nightmarish this year."

data.title: vVARDIS and Henry Schein One Launch One-Click Auto Charting for Early-Stage Cavity Care
data.description:
vVARDIS and Henry Schein One Launch One-Click Auto Charting for Early-Stage Cavity Care

A new feature inside Dentrix and Ascend by Dentrix automatically charts early-stage cavity treatment and includes drill-free Curodont® Repair Fluoride Plus as a treatment option.

vVARDIS (NYSE: VVVV), the Swiss healthcare company in the dental med-tech sector offering non-invasive treatment for early-stage cavities, and Henry Schein One, a global leader in dental technology, today announced the launch of clinical auto-charting functionality for clinicians documenting early-stage cavities.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261127771676/en/

When a clinician detects an early-stage cavity, auto-charting features in Dentrix and Ascend record the code in the patient's chart with one click, reducing the charting process by 86%. The care team can then choose Curodont® to treat the tooth during the same visit, without duplicate documentation and with access to patient education resources regarding Curodont® within the platform. Throughout this workflow, treatment planning and decisions remain solely at the discretion of the clinician and patient.

The launch will represent the next phase of the collaboration between vVARDIS and Henry Schein One, which earlier this year introduced in-software awareness of Curodont® Repair Fluoride Plus to practices that use Dentrix and Ascend across the United States.

Tooth decay is the world’s most prevalent non-communicable disease, affecting approximately 2.5 billion people globally.1 A recent population-based cohort study in the U.S. associates untreated cavities with a 26 percent increased risk of all-cause mortality and a 48 percent increase in heart-disease mortality.2 Curodont® is designed as a non-invasive treatment intended to arrest or reverse early-stage cavities without drilling. Since its U.S. commercial launch in January 2024, vVARDIS estimates that Curodont® Repair Fluoride Plus has been used to treat over 3.5 million teeth and has been sold to over 20,000 of the approximately 110,000 general dental practices in the U.S., as of June 30, 2026.3

"Finding an early cavity and treating it should be one workflow, not two," said Haley Abivardi, DMD, co-CEO and co-founder of vVARDIS. “Dental teams want accurate information about their options for early-stage cavities, and patients want to understand the treatment they receive. This new functionality is another example of how technology is helping to create more efficiency in dental practices.”

"Our vision for Dentrix and Ascend is to bring intelligence directly into the clinical workflow, supporting clinicians without adding complexity. Auto-charting for the treatment of early-stage cavities is a great example of how we are connecting clinical insights, AI imaging, and documentation in a one click workflow to make technology work more simply for the dental team,” said April Lowry, Executive Director and General Manager, Clinical and AI, Henry Schein One.

This partnership promises to streamline access to drill-free dental solutions for patients across the United States.

“Dentrix and Ascend are part of the daily workflow for tens of thousands of U.S. practices,” said Greg Smith, Senior Vice President and General Manager, North America, vVARDIS. “We’re pleased to work with Henry Schein One to make information about Curodont® and drill-free treatment options for early-stage cavities more accessible to dental practices.”

Availability

Dentrix and Ascend are used in more than 75,000 locations in the United States. Auto-charting and the in-software Curodont® content are expected to become available within the next 30 days. vVARDIS and Henry Schein One plan to demonstrate the integration at the Greater New York Dental Meeting in New York City, November 29 to December 2, 2026.

About vVARDIS

vVARDIS (NYSE: VVVV) is a Swiss healthcare company in the dental med-tech sector headquartered in Zug, Switzerland, founded by Drs. Haley and Goly Abivardi, sisters, internationally renowned dentists and serial entrepreneurs. The company’s proprietary Curodont® technology platform offers an early therapeutic solution for tooth decay. Its flagship products are based on proprietary, peptide-containing formulations that complement the patient’s natural biology to help it stop the progression of early-stage cavities, preserve natural tooth structure and repair damaged enamel in early-stage cavities. Curodont®’s underlying technology is supported by a body of scientific evidence accumulated over the last 25 years, published in more than 250 publications, including randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses and long-term real-world cohort analyses. Curodont® is featured in the curricula of over 50 U.S. and European dental programs. For more information, visit www.vVARDIS.com and ww.linkedin.com/company/vvardis.

About Henry Schein One

Henry Schein One, a global leader in dental technology, empowers dentists to focus on patient care and helps to ensure practice success. With simple and integrated technology, practices become more efficient, profitable, and connected—leading to better experiences for patients and care teams alike. The company’s comprehensive portfolio spans demand generation, patient experience, practice management, revenue cycle, analytics, and clinical workflow.

Henry Schein One, LLC, is a joint venture between Henry Schein, Inc. (Nasdaq: HSIC) and Internet Brands. Its brands include Dentrix, Ascend by Dentrix, Jarvis Analytics, TechCentral, Lighthouse360, and DentalPlans.com, as well as international brands such as Dentally and Software of Excellence.

data.title: AHF: New Policy Brief Charts Path to African Health Sovereignty
data.description:
AHF: New Policy Brief Charts Path to African Health Sovereignty

Amid declining international health funding and Africa’s continued dependence on foreign medical supply chains, the AIDS Healthcare Foundation (AHF) Global Public Health Institute, the University of Miami Public Health Policy Lab, and the United Nations University Institute on Comparative Regional Integration Studies (UNU-CRIS) launched a new policy brief on advancing African health sovereignty on Nov. 25 at the second African Health Leader Dialogue during the Fifth International Conference on Public Health in Africa (CPHIA) in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

The policy brief, Operationalising Health Sovereignty in Africa: From Political Commitments to Regional Manufacturing of Medical Products, published by UNU-CRIS, calls for greater African control over health financing, medical manufacturing, and global health decision-making and outlines six recommendations to translate political commitments into action:

  • Support African health institutions. Provide clear mandates, sustained funding, and public accountability mechanisms.
  • Sustain African production through regional markets. Link pooled procurement, reliable payments, regulatory cooperation, and regional trade to equitable access to African-made medical products.
  • Finance African-defined health priorities. Commit predictable domestic and regional funding to services, preparedness, and manufacturing.
  • Strengthen diagnostics and data sovereignty. Invest in diagnostic production and laboratory networks while safeguarding African control over surveillance data.
  • Retain African scientific capability. Fund African-led research, build sustainable scientific career pathways, and negotiate rights to manufacture health technologies locally.
  • Negotiate partnerships collectively. Align external support with African priorities and leverage regional bargaining power to secure enforceable benefit sharing and equitable access to medical products.

The COVID-19 pandemic and recent cuts to international health funding, including disruptions to HIV services in 2025, have exposed the urgent need for sustainable, African-led health systems. African governments continue to fall short of their Abuja Declaration commitment to allocate at least 15% of national budgets to health, while achieving the African Union’s target of locally producing 60% of vaccines used on the continent by 2040 requires sustained investment and regional cooperation.

The brief also identifies ongoing negotiations on the World Health Organization Pandemic Agreement’s Pathogen Access and Benefit-Sharing (PABS) annex as an opportunity for African countries to collectively secure equitable access to vaccines, diagnostics, therapeutics, and other medical products.

The brief grew out of discussions among African health leaders in Accra, Ghana, in December 2025 as part of the AHF-funded Building Regional Integration for Distributed Governance of Epidemics (BRIDGE) Study, which examines how regional cooperation can prevent, prepare for, and respond to outbreaks, epidemics, and pandemics.

Read the full policy brief here.

AIDS Healthcare Foundation (AHF), the world’s largest HIV/AIDS healthcare organization, provides cutting-edge medicine and advocacy to more than 3.3 million people across 50 countries, including the U.S. and in Africa, Latin America/Caribbean, the Asia/Pacific Region, and Eastern Europe. In January 2025, AHF received the MLK, Jr. Social Justice Award, The King Center’s highest recognition for an organization leading work in the social justice arena. To learn more about AHF, visit us online at AIDShealth.org, find us on Facebook, and follow us on Instagram, Twitter, and TikTok.

The AHF Global Public Health Institute is an initiative of the AIDS Healthcare Foundation created to engage in global public health policy analysis and research to generate objective evidence that can inform improvements in public health policy at the global, regional, national, and local levels, particularly for infectious diseases. To learn more about the AHF Global Public Health Institute, visit https://ahfinstitute.org/.

The University of Miami Public Health Policy Lab is dedicated to advancing research, policy analysis, and collaborative initiatives that strengthen public health systems globally, with a particular focus on the Global South. Through interdisciplinary research, stakeholder engagement, and evidence-driven policy recommendations, the lab addresses critical challenges in global health governance, regional health cooperation, and infectious disease response. Our work informs strategies to enhance health equity, pandemic preparedness, and integrated health systems, fostering regional and international collaboration. To learn more about the UM Public Health Policy Lab, visit https://www.publichealth.med.miami.edu/research/research-labs/umphpl/index.html or to view our previous webinar and event recordings visit https://www.youtube.com/@MiamiPolicyLab.

data.title: Precious Metals Rally as AI Trade Revives Risk Appetite — Update
data.description:
By Giulia Petroni and Adam Whittaker

Precious-metal prices surged Friday as investors returned to the artificial-intelligence trade and global stocks rebounded, boosting risk appetite and easing pressure on assets that had been sold to meet liquidity needs.

Copper futures rose 3.4% Friday to $5.5170 a pound.

The rally also lifted mining stocks in London, with the sector leading gains on the FTSE 100. Friday's advance follows a challenging period for mining companies, whose shares have come under pressure as metal prices weakened and concerns about the AI trade weighed on investor sentiment.

Silver and gold miner Fresnillo shares rose 4.8%, while its peer Endeavour Mining gained 3.1%. Copper producer Antofagasta climbed 4.4%. Diversified miners Glencore and Anglo American, both with significant exposure to copper, advanced 4.3% and 3.8%, respectively. Valterra Platinum's London-listed shares gained 7.8%.

"Beyond the technical nature of the rebound, the recovery also highlights the role of precious metals as an ATM in times of market stress," analysts at Saxo Bank said. "With AI-related technology stocks rebounding and broader risk appetite improving, the queue at the cash machine appears to be thinning, easing the liquidity-driven selling pressure."

Still, the broader macroeconomic backdrop remains challenging. Traders are pricing in a quarter-point rate hike at the Federal Reserve's next policy meeting in December, while attention is also turning to whether the U.S. central bank will signal further monetary tightening for 2027.

Higher interest rates can weigh on nonyielding assets such as gold and silver by making interest-bearing investments relatively more attractive.

data.title: Mall of America® makes Black Friday history with a GUINNESS WORLD RECORDS® title
data.description:
Mall of America® makes Black Friday history with a GUINNESS WORLD RECORDS® title

Mall of America® makes Black Friday history with a GUINNESS WORLD RECORDS® title

PR Newswire

BLOOMINGTON, Minn., Nov. 27, 2026

More than 15,000 guests arrive in the first hour of opening as MOA launches the holiday season with $100,000 in prizes and giveaways

BLOOMINGTON, Minn., Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Mall of America® made history this Black Friday, setting a GUINNESS WORLD RECORDS® title for the most people holding up the same shopping bag simultaneously. The milestone kicked off a day of holiday excitement featuring more than $100,000 in prizes and giveaways, exclusive deals and live entertainment.

 Mall of America® makes Black Friday history with GUINNESS WORLD RECORDS® title.

For Black Friday b-roll, photos and sound bites, please visit: Black Friday 2026
(In timelapse video, GUINNESS WORLD RECORDS at 01:33)

Black Friday at a Glance:

  • New record: 854 guests officially held up the same shopping bag simultaneously, and an official adjudicator confirmed the GUINNESS WORLD RECORDS title.
  • Early-morning excitement: More than 15,000 shoppers entered Mall of America within the first hour of opening at 7 a.m. Guests began lining up at the North Entrance as early as 10:30 a.m. on Thanksgiving Day.
  • Giveaways: Eligible entrants received an exclusive shopping bag filled with giveaways valued at $100 or more.
  • What's in the bag: The MOA® bags given to entrants for the GUINNESS WORLD RECORDS title included a variety of gifts, gift cards and a Mystery Scratch-Off card presented by Minnesota Lottery.
    • Mystery Scratch-Off prizes ranged from $10 to $599.99. Some of the big prizes included a gaming console, smartwatch, hotel stays and more.
  • Shopping sprees: Three lucky eligible entrants participating in the GUINNESS WORLD RECORDS title won shopping sprees valued at $5,000, $2,500 and $1,000.

"Black Friday at Mall of America is one of our most anticipated traditions. It brings together the excitement of holiday shopping, the energy of the day and memories our guests look forward to making year after year," said Jill Renslow, Chief Business Development & Marketing Officer at Mall of America. "Creating unique experiences has always been at the heart of who we are. This year, we brought that spirit to life in an extraordinary way by inviting our guests to be part of a record-setting moment. There's no better way to kick off the holiday season than by making history together."

The record attempt was one of the morning's highlights. 1,000 eligible guests raised their shopping bags in unison. A GUINNESS WORLD RECORDS adjudicator verified the achievement of 854 valid participants. The record was celebrated with streamers, music and cheers from the crowd.

Three eligible entrants who participated in the record attempt were surprised by being invited onstage to receive symbolic oversized checks for their shopping sprees:

  • $5,000 in Mall of America gift cards
  • $2,500 in Mall of America gift cards
  • A $1,000 lululemon gift card, courtesy of lululemon

This year's celebration also marks 10 years since Mall of America made the industry-leading decision to close on Thanksgiving Day, giving team members and retail employees time with family and friends before welcoming shoppers on Black Friday.

From a world-record attempt to major giveaways, this year's Black Friday brought thousands of guests together to kick off the holiday shopping season. The celebration reflected Mall of America's combination of shopping, entertainment and experiences that bring people together year after year.

For more information on Black Friday weekend deals, attractions and events, visit mallofamerica.com/blackfriday.

data.title: World Tennis and Generali seal new expanded partnership to power global participation
data.description:
World Tennis and Generali seal new expanded partnership to power global participation

World Tennis and Generali seal new expanded partnership to power global participation

PR Newswire

BOLOGNA, Italy, Nov. 27, 2026
  • Targeting global player growth of +20 million by 2035
  • Goal to introduce tennis to over 1 million young people annually

BOLOGNA, Italy, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- World Tennis and Generali have signed a new and amplified multi-year partnership to expand the global growth of tennis and build more active communities worldwide.

The deal enhances the collaboration between the organisations, following the announcement of Generali's landmark Davis Cup presenting partnership in September.

The expanded agreement will bring significant investment into flagship World Tennis programmes that empower people to enjoy the sport from the Junior Tennis Initiative to the Masters Tour, as well as national tennis infrastructure, coach development, mass participation and new grassroots initiatives.

The partnership is built on a shared belief in the power of physical activity to improve lives and support longevity while concretely helping to build towards World Tennis' global participation growth target of +20 million tennis players by 2035.*

Generali has strong foundations in supporting active lifestyles across tennis, running, football and winter sports. In tennis this includes title sponsorship of the Generali Open in Kitzbühel and a partnership with Dominic Thiem in Austria, sponsorship of the Rolex Monte Carlo Masters event and partnerships with the Real Federación Española de Tenis (RFET) and Deutsche Tennis Bund (DTB), as well as the global presenting partnership with Davis Cup announced in September.

In line with Generali's Lifetime Partner proposition, the Group strongly believes that people who are more active and more connected live healthier, happier and more fulfilling lives. Generali's targeted sports partnerships allow the Group to bring this belief to life, creating opportunities for people to move more by removing barriers to participation and encouraging healthier lifestyles. This also brings people together, creating meaningful connections and strengthening communities through shared experiences, ultimately helping everyone live better everywhere the Group operates.

The partnership with World Tennis will support a range of grassroots initiatives, building on World Tennis' existing programmes, Junior and Masters initiatives, as well as developing new ones, all delivered in collaboration with World Tennis' vast global network of 214 member National Associations with the goal to make the sport more accessible and increase participation across ages supporting longevity, health, wellbeing and connections within communities.

*Based on projected growth from 106 million players in 2024 (reported in Global Tennis Data Report) and current trajectory towards World Tennis participation target of 140 million players by 2035.

Initial overview of relevant programmes

1)  Generali World Tennis Masters Tour

A truly global tennis community of over 42,000 players competing in over 650 events per year in 75 countries – including the prestigious World Team and Individual Championships. The focus is on providing opportunities for players aged 30-100. Through this partnership, World Tennis is targeting a 10% increase in tournaments and players in 2027 and further growth from 2028 onwards.

2)  Generali Junior Tennis Initiative

Through World Tennis' global network of National Associations, 131 countries are currently supported through the Junior Tennis Initiative (JTI). The JTI provides young people with their first opportunity to experience tennis through schools, clubs and local communities. Together with Generali, World Tennis will expand the influence of the JTI in more countries in 2027, with a goal to introduce tennis to over one-million young people annually.

3)  Generali Coaches For Life

Support for and access to coach education programmes and scholarships that empower the mentors behind every player.

4)  Generali World Tennis Activation

Mass participation initiatives in key Generali markets through the February and September Davis Cup by Generali ties; turning the prestigious global event into a local engagement opportunity.

5)  Generali Rally Together Fund

Ringfenced funding for investment into new tennis facilities, infrastructure and national training centres across the world.

Ross Hutchins, World Tennis Chief Executive, said: "We are proud to deepen our collaboration with Generali, which is based on shared core values and a belief in the power of physical activity. Our Davis Cup partnership already allows meaningful engagement with local communities and nations across the world. This expanded new agreement will further empower our flagship programmes that support people to access our sport and its proven health benefits regardless of age, gender or background. Generali strongly believes in the potential of those programmes in line with their commitment to support physical wellbeing to strengthen connection and belonging in communities.

"When we became World Tennis this year, we stated our mission: to create a world of opportunities through tennis both on and off the court. We know that tennis can build stronger communities and allows people to live healthier, happier, longer lives worldwide. Now we have the chance to further harness that power as we build towards our target of 20 million new players by 2035."

Generali Group CEO, Philippe Donnet, said: "As a Lifetime Partner, Generali is committed to helping people build a more secure and sustainable future by supporting initiatives that enhance wellbeing and strengthen communities. Sponsorships play an important role in this commitment, providing meaningful opportunities to connect with people through shared passions and experiences. Among the many sports we support, tennis stands out for its universal appeal, strong values and positive impact on physical and mental wellbeing across all generations.

"The new and expanded partnership with World Tennis marks an important step in combining our support for high level competitions with grassroots initiatives that create opportunities for many more people to play, connect and thrive through sport. Together with World Tennis, we look forward to helping grow the game and contributing to healthier, more connected communities that can live better, and longer lives."
